name: Consolidated - DEP
headers: Clear and easy to understand policy statement
rows: The Accountable Authority determines their entity's tolerance for security risks and documents in the security plan.
Sets the risk tolerance boundary for all digital experience, collaboration and end user computing decisions, including what residual security risk can be accepted.
High - applies across all three policy scopes because NDIA digital channels, staff collaboration platforms and managed devices process government information and participant/provider data.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - security risk governance and accountability

NDIA must align digital experience channels, collaboration platforms and end user computing environments with documented entity security risk tolerances and record any residual-risk acceptance in the security plan or an approved risk artefact.
A risk steward (or manager) is identified for each security risk or category of security risk, including shared risks.
Ensures named ownership for security risks and shared risks affecting digital services, productivity platforms and devices.
High - applies across all three scopes; risk ownership is required for digital channels, M365/recordkeeping platforms, EUC devices and supplier dependencies.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - security risk governance and accountability

NDIA must assign a risk steward or manager for each security risk category affecting the Digital Experience, Collaboration and Productivity, and End User Computing scopes, including shared risks with suppliers or other entities.
The Accountable Authority considers the impact that their security risk management decisions could potentially have on other entities, and shares information on risks where appropriate.
Requires the policy to consider downstream security impacts on other entities when digital services, shared platforms or access arrangements change.
High - applies to cross-government services, provider interactions, inter-agency collaboration and shared technology dependencies.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - cross-entity risk management
NDIA digital and ICT decisions must assess potential security impacts on other entities and share relevant risk information through agreed governance, procurement and assurance channels.

The entity is accountable for the management of security risks arising from procuring goods and services and ensures procurement and contract decisions do not expose the entity or the Australian Government to an unacceptable level of risk.
NDIA digital experiences, collaboration tools and EUC services rely on third parties; procurement and contract decisions must not introduce unacceptable security risk.
High - applies to outsourced SaaS, cloud, device, support, integration and digital channel providers.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - third-party digital services and supplier assurance

NDIA remains accountable for security risks arising from procured digital services and must assess and approve supplier risk before onboarding platforms, devices, support services or digital channels.

Procurement, contracts and third-party outsourced arrangements contain proportionate security terms and conditions to ensure service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements.
Contracts for digital channels, collaboration platforms, EUC devices and support must contain enforceable PSPF security terms.
High - applies to suppliers delivering or supporting public channels, staff collaboration services, content platforms, devices and managed services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - third-party digital services and supplier assurance

All relevant procurements and contracts for digital experience, collaboration and EUC services must include proportionate security, privacy, incident reporting, access, recordkeeping and PSPF compliance obligations.
Entity ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors comply with relevant PSPF Requirements as detailed by the entity.
Ensures service providers, contractors and subcontractors supporting the policy scopes follow NDIA-specified PSPF obligations.
High - applies to all contracted providers and subcontractors that design, host, support, manage or access NDIA digital and EUC environments.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - third-party digital services and supplier assurance

Service providers, contractors and subcontractors supporting NDIA digital experience, collaboration or EUC services must comply with NDIA security requirements and the relevant PSPF obligations specified by NDIA.

Contractual security terms and conditions require service providers to report any actual or suspected security incidents to the entity, and follow reasonable direction from the entity arising from incident investigations.
Supplier incident reporting must be built into arrangements for platforms, devices, identities, content and participant/provider data.
High - applies to suppliers with access to NDIA systems, information, collaboration content, devices or service management functions.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - supplier incident reporting and cooperation

Supplier contracts must require prompt reporting of actual or suspected security incidents affecting NDIA digital services, collaboration content, devices, identities or data, and require cooperation with NDIA investigations and directions.
Government entities providing outsourced services provide IRAP assessment reports to the government entities consuming, or looking to consume, their services.
IRAP reporting supports assurance and authorisation decisions for outsourced ICT services consumed by NDIA.
High where NDIA consumes government-provided, shared or outsourced ICT services supporting the three policy scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - assurance evidence and IRAP reporting

Where NDIA consumes outsourced government services or assessed ICT services, the service owner or provider must make current IRAP assessment information available to support NDIA authorisation, assurance and risk decisions.

Contract security terms and conditions are monitored and reviewed to ensure the specified security controls, terms and conditions are implemented, operated and maintained by the contracted provider, including any subcontractors, over the life of a contract.
Ongoing contract monitoring is needed to keep provider controls effective over the life of digital, collaboration and EUC arrangements.
High - applies to contracted providers and subcontractors supporting in-scope platforms, integrations, devices or services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - contract monitoring and control assurance

NDIA must monitor contracted providers and subcontractors throughout the contract term to confirm agreed controls, access protections, recordkeeping requirements and incident obligations remain implemented and effective.
Contractual terms and conditions include appropriate security arrangements for the completion or termination of the contract.
Secure exit and transition requirements are necessary to protect information, records, devices and access when digital service contracts end.
High - applies to service completion, transition, renewal or termination for digital platforms, collaboration services, managed devices and support contracts.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - supplier exit and transition controls

Contracts supporting NDIA digital platforms, collaboration services and EUC environments must define secure exit, data return or destruction, access removal, asset return, records transfer and knowledge-transfer requirements.
Procurement and contract decisions consider the security risks before engaging providers operating under foreign ownership, control or influence.
Foreign ownership, control or influence can affect supplier access to NDIA systems, staff work output and participant/provider information.
High - applies before engaging providers that may access, host, support or influence digital experience, collaboration or EUC services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - foreign ownership, control or influence risk

Before engaging providers under foreign ownership, control or influence, NDIA must assess security risks to participant, provider, staff and government information and obtain risk acceptance at the appropriate authority.
Security risks arising from contractual arrangements for the provision of goods and services are managed, reassessed and adjusted over the life of a contract.
Supplier risks change over time as scope, architecture, subcontractors, data locations and threats change.
High - applies over the full lifecycle of digital, collaboration and EUC supplier arrangements.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - supplier lifecycle risk management

Security risks in digital supplier arrangements must be reviewed and updated over the contract lifecycle, including when service scope, architecture, subcontractors, data location or threat conditions change.
Secure and verifiable third-party vendors, providers, partners and associated services are used unless business operations require use, and the residual risks are managed and approved by the CISO.
Digital service integrity depends on secure and verifiable third-party vendors and approved residual risk where exceptions are needed.
High - applies to digital platforms, SaaS, endpoint tools, collaboration services, device suppliers and associated support services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - secure and verifiable vendor use

NDIA must use secure and verifiable third-party vendors and associated services for digital experience, collaboration and EUC capabilities unless an approved business need exists and the CISO approves the residual risk.
The originator remains responsible for controlling the sanitisation, reclassification or declassification of official and security classified information.
Digital policy must preserve originator control over sanitisation, reclassification and declassification when information is created, shared or reused.
High - applies to content created or shared through participant/provider channels, productivity tools, repositories and staff devices.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - information classification, markings and recordkeeping

Originators of NDIA official and security classified information must retain responsibility for sanitisation, reclassification and declassification before information is published, shared, reused or disposed of in digital channels or collaboration platforms.

The value, importance or sensitivity of official information is assessed by the originator by considering the potential damage to the government, the national interest, organisations or individuals that would arise if the information's confidentiality were compromised.
Information in digital channels and staff platforms must be assessed for sensitivity before it is published, shared, stored or reused.
High - applies to participant, provider, staff, corporate and government information handled through all three scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - information classification, markings and recordkeeping

NDIA staff and contractors creating or handling information in digital services, collaboration repositories or EUC environments must assess value, importance and sensitivity before sharing, storing or publishing information.
The security classification is set at the lowest reasonable level.
The policy must avoid over-classification while ensuring information receives appropriate protection in digital systems.
High - applies to content, records, email, collaboration workspaces, public content preparation and device storage.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - information classification, markings and recordkeeping
NDIA must apply the lowest reasonable security classification to information while ensuring required protections are maintained in digital channels, collaboration workspaces and records repositories.

Security classified information is clearly marked with the applicable security classification, and when relevant, security caveat, by using text-based markings, unless impractical for operational reasons.
Classified information must remain identifiable when it moves through digital systems, documents, emails and collaboration platforms.
High - applies where security classified information is created, stored, processed, communicated or displayed in in-scope services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - protective markings

Security classified information in NDIA digital systems, emails, documents and collaboration spaces must be clearly text-marked with the applicable classification and caveat unless impractical for operational reasons.
The minimum protections and handling requirements are applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information.
Minimum protections must be embedded into how digital channels, productivity services and devices handle OFFICIAL and classified information.
High - applies to all policy scopes because NDIA systems and devices process OFFICIAL and potentially security classified information.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - information protection controls
NDIA digital channels, collaboration platforms and EUC environments must apply the minimum protections and handling requirements for OFFICIAL and security classified information.
The Australian Government Security Caveat Standard and special handling requirements imposed by the controlling authority are applied to protect security caveated information.
Caveated information has additional handling obligations that must be supported in digital workflows and collaboration spaces.
Conditional but mandatory when caveated information is stored, processed, communicated or displayed in NDIA systems.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - caveat handling

NDIA must apply Australian Government caveat standards and any controlling-authority handling requirements to caveated information stored, processed, communicated or displayed through digital services or staff platforms.
Security caveats are clearly marked as text and only appear in conjunction with a security classification.
Caveat markings must be clear and consistently applied to prevent inappropriate digital sharing or access.
Conditional but mandatory when caveated security classified information is handled in NDIA systems or outputs.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - caveat marking rules
Security caveats must be text-marked and used only with a security classification in NDIA digital content, records, emails and collaboration outputs.
Accountable material has page and reference numbering.
Accountable material requires traceability when produced, shared or stored through digital collaboration and records processes.
Conditional - applies when NDIA creates, handles or stores accountable material in digital or printed form.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope - accountable material controls
Where NDIA handles accountable material in digital or printed form, pages and reference numbers must be applied and maintained in collaboration, publishing and recordkeeping processes.
Accountable material is handled in accordance with any special handling requirements imposed by the originator and security caveat owner.
Special handling rules for accountable material must follow the information owner through digital workflows and staff devices.
Conditional - applies when accountable material is handled in digital collaboration, records, publishing or EUC environments.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - accountable material controls
Accountable material in NDIA digital channels, collaboration workspaces or EUC environments must be handled according to any originator or caveat-owner special handling requirements.

The Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard is applied to protect OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged by email in and between Australian Government entities, including other authorised parties.
Email remains a core collaboration channel and must support protective marking for OFFICIAL and classified information exchange.
High - applies to NDIA email and authorised productivity tools used with government entities and other authorised parties.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope - email protective marking

NDIA email services and authorised productivity tools must support and enforce the Australian Government Email Protective Marking Standard for OFFICIAL and security classified information exchanged within government and with authorised parties.

The Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Security Classification' property (and where relevant, the 'Security Caveat' property) is applied to protectively mark information on technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information.
Recordkeeping metadata is required so systems can mark and protect classified records consistently.
High where NDIA systems store, process or communicate security classified information in records, document or collaboration repositories.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope - recordkeeping metadata and protective marking

NDIA technology systems that store, process or communicate security classified information must support recordkeeping metadata for Security Classification and, where relevant, Security Caveat properties.
Apply the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard's 'Rights' property where the entity wishes to categorise information content by the type of restrictions on access.
Access restriction metadata supports controlled collaboration and lawful reuse of NDIA information.
High where NDIA needs to categorise content by access restrictions in records, repositories or collaboration platforms.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope - access restriction metadata

Where NDIA restricts access to information content, collaboration and records systems must support the Australian Government Recordkeeping Metadata Standard Rights property or equivalent access-restriction metadata.
Security classified discussions and dissemination of security classified information are only conducted in approved locations.
Classified discussions and dissemination must only occur from approved environments, including when digital meeting tools are used.
High where classified discussions or dissemination occur through collaboration tools, meetings, messaging or remote work arrangements.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - approved locations for classified discussions

Security classified discussions and dissemination through NDIA collaboration tools, meetings, messaging or other channels must occur only from approved locations and environments suitable for the classification.
Entity implements operational controls for its information holdings that are proportional to their value, importance and sensitivity.
Digital experience and collaboration platforms hold valuable participant, provider, staff and corporate information requiring proportional controls.
High - applies to information holdings across public channels, business systems, records, collaboration repositories, logs and managed devices.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - information holdings and operational controls

NDIA must implement operational controls for information holdings in digital channels, collaboration repositories and EUC environments that are proportionate to the information's value, importance and sensitivity.

OFFICIAL and security classified information is disposed of securely in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements, ISM, the Records Authorities, a Normal Administrative Practice and the Archives Act 1983.
Digital platforms and devices must dispose of OFFICIAL and classified information securely and consistently with records obligations.
High - applies to documents, workspace content, logs, files, messages, data extracts, storage media and device data.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - retention, disposal and secure destruction

NDIA must dispose of OFFICIAL and security classified information in collaboration platforms, digital services and EUC environments according to minimum handling requirements, the ISM, records authorities, normal administrative practice and the Archives Act.

Security classified information is appropriately destroyed in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements when it has passed the minimum retention requirements or reaches authorised destruction dates.
Security classified information requires authorised destruction only after retention requirements are met.
High where NDIA stores or handles security classified information in repositories, collaboration platforms, removable media or devices.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - secure destruction of classified information

Security classified information held in NDIA digital repositories, removable media or devices must be destroyed only when retention requirements or authorised destruction dates are met and approved destruction methods are used.

Access to security classified information or resources is only provided to people outside the entity with the appropriate security clearance (where required) and a need-to-know, and is transferred in accordance with the Minimum Protections and Handling Requirements.
External digital sharing must restrict access to classified information to cleared people with need to know and approved transfer mechanisms.
High where NDIA shares security classified information or resources with people outside the entity.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - secure information sharing and external collaboration

NDIA must share security classified information or resources outside the entity only with people who hold required clearances, have a need to know, and use approved transfer methods and minimum protections.
The Memorandum of Understanding between the Commonwealth, States and Territories is applied when sharing information with state and territory government agencies.
NDIA exchanges information with state and territory partners; digital and collaboration arrangements must reflect whole-of-government sharing rules.
High where NDIA shares information with state and territory agencies through portals, email, collaboration spaces or integrations.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - intergovernmental information sharing

When NDIA shares information with state or territory government agencies, digital sharing arrangements must apply the Commonwealth, States and Territories information-sharing MOU and any NDIA-specific controls.
An agreement or arrangement is in place before security classified information or resources are disclosed or shared with a person or organisation outside of government.
Agreements or arrangements are needed before digital collaboration with non-government parties involving security classified information.
Conditional but mandatory where NDIA shares security classified information or resources outside government.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - external collaboration agreements

Before security classified information is disclosed to people or organisations outside government through digital channels or collaboration services, NDIA must establish an agreement or arrangement covering security obligations.
Provisions are met concerning the security of people, information and resources contained in international agreements and arrangements to which Australia is a party.
International agreements may impose security controls on digital sharing, collaboration and remote access arrangements.
Conditional - applies where NDIA participates in international agreements or arrangements, or shares information/resources internationally.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - international information sharing
Where an international agreement or arrangement applies, NDIA digital sharing and collaboration processes must meet provisions for protecting people, information and resources.

Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign entity is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
Foreign entity sharing requires a legal or international authority and protective arrangements.
Conditional - applies if NDIA shares Australian Government security classified information or resources with a foreign entity.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - foreign entity information sharing

NDIA must share Australian Government security classified information or resources with a foreign entity only where an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement authorises and protects the sharing.

Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AUSTEO caveat is never shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, even when an international agreement or arrangement is in place, unless an exemption is granted.
AUSTEO controls must be enforceable in digital sharing and collaboration workflows.
Conditional - applies when AUSTEO information or resources are handled in NDIA systems or shared processes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - AUSTEO caveat controls
NDIA systems and collaboration processes must prevent AUSTEO information or resources from being shared with non-Australian citizens unless an authorised exemption has been granted.
Australian Government security classified information or resources bearing the AGAO caveat is not shared with a person who is not an Australian citizen, except as specified.
AGAO controls must be enforceable in digital sharing and collaboration workflows.
Conditional - applies when AGAO information or resources are handled in NDIA systems or shared processes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - AGAO caveat controls

NDIA systems and collaboration processes must restrict AGAO information or resources from being shared with non-Australian citizens except where permitted by the caveat rules and authorised arrangements.

Where an international agreement or arrangement is in place, security classified foreign entity information or resources are safeguarded in accordance with the provisions set out in the agreement or arrangement.
Foreign entity information must be protected when stored, processed or communicated through NDIA digital systems.
Conditional - applies where NDIA receives security classified information or resources from a foreign entity under an agreement or arrangement.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - safeguarding foreign entity information

NDIA must safeguard foreign entity security classified information or resources according to the relevant international agreement or arrangement when stored, processed or communicated through NDIA digital platforms.

Australian Government security classified information or resources shared with a foreign non-government stakeholder is protected by an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
Sharing with foreign non-government stakeholders must be legally authorised and protected by an appropriate arrangement.
Conditional - applies if NDIA shares Australian Government security classified information or resources with foreign non-government stakeholders.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - foreign non-government stakeholder sharing

NDIA must share Australian Government security classified information or resources with foreign non-government stakeholders only under an explicit legislative provision, international agreement or international arrangement.
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual cyber security principles are applied during all stages of the lifecycle of each system.
Digital services, productivity platforms and EUC environments are technology systems; their lifecycle must be governed by ISM cyber security principles.
High - applies across all three policy scopes and supporting technology platforms.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - technology lifecycle, authorisation and secure-by-design
NDIA must apply ASD ISM cyber security principles across the lifecycle of digital experience channels, collaboration platforms, end user devices and supporting technology systems.
The Australian Signals Directorate's Information Security Manual controls and cyber security guidelines are applied on a risk-based approach.
The policy must require risk-based selection and implementation of ISM controls for digital, collaboration and EUC systems.
High - applies to design, procurement, configuration, operation and change of in-scope technology systems.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - ISM control implementation

NDIA must select and apply ASD ISM controls and cyber security guidelines to Digital Experience, Collaboration and Productivity, and End User Computing services using a documented risk-based approach.

The Authorising Officer authorises each technology system to operate based on the acceptance of the residual security risks associated with its operation before that system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
Digital and staff-facing systems must not operate with government information until residual security risk is authorised.
High - applies before any in-scope technology system processes, stores or communicates government information or data.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - authorisation to operate

Each NDIA technology system supporting digital experience, collaboration or EUC must be authorised to operate by an Authorising Officer based on acceptance of residual security risks before processing, storing or communicating government information.
Decisions to authorise (or reauthorise) a new technology system or make changes to an existing technology system are based on the ISM's risk-based approach to cyber security.
New systems and significant changes need reauthorisation based on cyber security risk, not only project delivery readiness.
High - applies to new or changed digital channels, collaboration services, devices, infrastructure, integrations and security tooling.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - change authorisation and reauthorisation
New systems and significant changes to existing NDIA digital, collaboration or EUC systems must be authorised or reauthorised using the ISM risk-based approach to cyber security.
The technology system is authorised to the highest security classification of the information and data it will process, store or communicate.
System authorisation must reflect the highest classification of information processed, stored or communicated.
High - applies to public digital channels, staff collaboration repositories, back-end systems and EUC environments.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - classification-based system authorisation

NDIA technology systems must be authorised to the highest security classification of the information or data they process, store or communicate, including public channels, staff collaboration repositories and EUC environments.

A register of the entity's authorised technology systems is developed, implemented and maintained, and includes the name and position of the Authorising Officer, system owner, date of authorisation, and any decisions to accept residual security risks.
A register is needed to maintain visibility of authorised digital, collaboration and EUC systems and accepted residual risks.
High - applies to in-scope applications, platforms, devices, services and supporting infrastructure.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - authorised systems register
NDIA must maintain a register of authorised digital, collaboration and EUC systems that records the Authorising Officer, system owner, authorisation date and any residual-risk acceptance decisions.

Each technology system's suitability to be authorised to operate is reassessed when it undergoes significant functionality or architectural change, or where the system's security environment has changed considerably.
Authorisations must remain current when systems, architectures or the threat environment change materially.
High - applies to significant functionality, architectural or security-environment changes affecting in-scope systems.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - periodic and event-driven reassessment
NDIA must reassess authorisation suitability for digital, collaboration and EUC systems when significant functionality, architectural or security-environment changes occur.
The TikTok application is prevented from being installed, and existing instances are removed, on government devices, unless a legitimate business reason exists.
EUC policy must prohibit high-risk applications on government devices unless approved; TikTok is specifically mandated.
High - applies to NDIA government devices used by staff and authorised contractors.
End User Computing Scope - managed device and application controls

NDIA must prevent the TikTok application from being installed on government devices and remove existing instances unless a legitimate business need has been approved through the required exception process.
The CSO or CISO approves any legitimate business reason for the use of the TikTok application on government devices and ensures specified mitigations are in place.
Exceptions for TikTok on government devices require senior security approval and mitigations.
High - applies to any NDIA business case seeking TikTok access or installation on a government device.
End User Computing Scope - high-risk application exceptions
Any legitimate business reason to use TikTok on an NDIA government device must be approved by the CSO or CISO and supported by specified mitigations before use.
The Australian Signals Directorate's temporary mitigations for legacy IT are applied to manage legacy information technology that cannot yet be replaced.
Legacy systems in digital channels and EUC environments can create unmanaged risk; policy must require ASD temporary mitigations.
High - applies to legacy technology that cannot yet be replaced and supports any of the three policy scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - legacy technology risk and compensating controls
NDIA must apply ASD temporary mitigations to manage legacy information technology supporting digital experience, collaboration or EUC services until the technology is remediated or replaced.
Technology assets are disposed of securely in accordance with the Information Security Manual.
End user devices, storage media and technology assets must be securely disposed of to protect NDIA and government information.
High - applies to end user devices, storage media, platform components and other technology assets used in the policy scopes.
End User Computing Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - technology asset disposal
NDIA must securely dispose of technology assets, including end user devices, storage media and platform components, in accordance with the ASD ISM and approved NDIA disposal processes.
Patch applications mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Application patching reduces compromise risk for public-facing digital channels, staff productivity tools and EUC endpoints.
High - applies to applications supporting digital experience, collaboration and managed end user environments.
End User Computing Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; Digital Experience Scope - Essential Eight baseline controls

NDIA must implement application patching for digital platforms, productivity applications and end user environments to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, or the approved target maturity where higher.
Patch operating systems mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Operating system patching is a baseline cyber control for servers, managed devices and supporting platforms.
High - applies to operating systems on devices, servers and platforms supporting all three policy scopes.
End User Computing Scope; Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - Essential Eight baseline controls
NDIA must implement operating system patching for servers, managed devices and supporting platforms to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, or the approved target maturity where higher.
Multi-factor authentication mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Multi-factor authentication is necessary to protect access to digital services, collaboration content, devices and administrative functions.
High - applies to user, privileged and remote access across all three policy scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - identity, authentication and MFA

NDIA must implement multi-factor authentication for access to digital services, collaboration platforms, administrative functions and EUC environments to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two, or the approved target maturity where higher.
Restrict administrative privileges mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Administrative privileges present high risk and must be restricted across platforms, applications, devices and support functions.
High - applies to system administrators, service owners, support teams and privileged accounts across all three policy scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - privileged access management

NDIA must restrict administrative privileges for digital systems, collaboration platforms and EUC environments to authorised roles, with approvals, monitoring and regular review aligned to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Application control mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Application control helps prevent unauthorised or malicious software execution on managed endpoints and servers.
High - primarily applies to managed end user devices and relevant servers supporting digital and collaboration services.
End User Computing Scope - application control
NDIA must implement application control on managed end user devices and relevant servers to prevent unauthorised software execution and meet at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Restrict Microsoft Office macros mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Microsoft Office macros are a common productivity-channel risk and must be restricted in staff collaboration environments.
High - applies to Microsoft Office, email and collaboration tools used by NDIA staff and authorised contractors.
Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - macro controls
NDIA must restrict Microsoft Office macros in productivity and collaboration environments to reduce malicious code risk and meet at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
User application hardening mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
User application hardening protects browsers, productivity applications and other user-facing software used across the digital workplace.
High - applies to browsers, email clients, productivity tools and other user applications in all three policy scopes.
End User Computing Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - user application hardening
NDIA must harden user applications used for digital experience, collaboration and EUC, including browsers and productivity tools, to meet at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.
Regular back-ups mitigation strategy is implemented to Maturity Level Two under ASD's Essential Eight Maturity Model.
Regular backups support resilience and recovery for digital services, collaboration content and staff computing environments.
High - applies to systems and information supporting public channels, staff platforms, records repositories and managed devices.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - resilience, backup and recovery
NDIA must maintain regular, protected and tested backups for systems and information supporting digital experience, collaboration and EUC services to at least Essential Eight Maturity Level Two.

The remaining mitigation strategies from the Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents are considered and, where required, implemented to achieve an acceptable level of residual risk for their entity.
The policy should require consideration of remaining ASD mitigation strategies where needed to achieve acceptable residual risk.
High - applies where additional mitigations are needed beyond the Essential Eight for the three policy scopes.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - cyber security mitigation strategy management

NDIA must consider the remaining ASD Strategies to Mitigate Cyber Security Incidents and implement those required to achieve an acceptable residual risk for digital experience, collaboration and EUC services.
A Protective Domain Name System service or other security mechanisms is used to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints.
Digital services and EUC environments need mechanisms to prevent connections to known malicious endpoints.
High - applies to internet-connected devices, applications, collaboration platforms and digital service infrastructure.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope; End User Computing Scope - network protection and malicious endpoint blocking
NDIA must use Protective Domain Name System services or equivalent security mechanisms to prevent connections to and from known malicious endpoints across digital, collaboration and EUC environments.
Cloud Service Providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest version of ASD's ISM within the previous 24 months are used.
Cloud collaboration and digital services must use independently assessed cloud providers to manage hosting and data security risk.
High - applies to cloud services used for digital channels, collaboration platforms, productivity tools and supporting ICT services.
Digital Experience Scope; Collaboration and Productivity Scope - cloud service provider assurance
NDIA must use cloud service providers that have completed an IRAP assessment against the latest ASD ISM within the previous 24 months for in-scope cloud digital experience and collaboration services.
Entities consider IRAP assessment recommendations and findings, and implement on a risk-based approach.
IRAP findings must be considered and treated before cloud and assessed services are accepted for use.
High - applies to IRAP-assessed digital, collaboration, cloud, gateway and EUC-related services.
